transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-05-19
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luca Ramirez (Redwood SE), Alyssa Park (NimbleDocs CTO), Jon Miller (NimbleDocs ML Eng), Priya Singh (NimbleDocs Security)

Summary (auto): demo + parity mapping, meet customer constraints re: latency and data residency.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining - I'm Maya, AE on the Redwood side. We have Luca here, our solutions engineer. How's everybody doing?
[00:08] Alyssa Park: Good, thanks. Excited to see how Redwood maps to our current OpenAI and Anthropic flows.
[00:13] Jon Miller: Quick note, we also run some models through Together for private endpoints, so parity there matters.
[00:18] Maya Chen: Great, we'll cover OpenAI/Anthropic/Together parity mapping, then a quick Console/Optimize walkthrough and finish with security and next steps. Sound good?
[00:25] Priya Singh: Yes, and we'll want to confirm SOC 2, KMS, and SSO details during the security section.

[02:10] Luca Ramirez: Cool, starting with the API mapping. Redwood exposes a unified REST/SDK interface for text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking. For OpenAI chat/completions mapping it's mostly one-to-one - we support chat messages + system/user roles, streaming responses, and function/tool calling. A couple of gotchas: tokenization differences can change cost/length calculations and sometimes you need to adjust max_tokens and stop sequences.
[02:40] Jon Miller: Tokenization differences - are we talking small variance or like 10-15%? In our tests OpenAI -> Together we saw about 8-12% delta depending on prompt.
[02:50] Luca Ramirez: Right, usually single-digit to low double-digit percent differences. We provide a tokenizer utility in the SDK to estimate token counts against the specific model variant.

[05:12] Maya Chen: On embeddings, Redwood supports both dense embeddings and re-ranking embeddings - the mapping for Anthropic/Cohere-style embeddings into Redwood is straightforward: endpoint name change plus vector dims may vary per open model. We can auto-normalize in the console.
[05:35] Alyssa Park: We rely heavily on embeddings for semantic search and vector store indexing - any migration friction here?
[05:42] Luca Ramirez: We recommend creating a small re-index window during PoC. Also Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization/precision profiles so you don't lose semantic quality when switching to a quantized model.

[07:30] Jon Miller: Streaming performance is a big deal - our user-facing UI waits for partial responses. Does Redwood support chunked streaming and partial updates?
[07:40] Luca Ramirez: Yes, full streaming is supported; function calling streams as well. There are options for chunk sizes and flush policies. For low-latency UI we suggest enabling continuous batching with small max batch sizes to preserve SLOs.

[10:05] Maya Chen: Quick Console walkthrough - you can pin model versions, set routing policies (latency/cost/region), create canary rollouts, and see token-level cost breakdowns. Also tracing hooks for per-request debug.
[10:28] Alyssa Park: Can we route by customer/team? We have multi-tenant usage in NimbleDocs so per-tenant routing would be useful.
[10:35] Luca Ramirez: Yes, you can set routing keys and policies - per-route dashboards show cost + latency. You can also configure automatic fallback to cheaper quantized variants if capacity or latency thresholds are hit.

[13:00] Priya Singh: Security - we need SOC 2 Type II, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS/HSM integration for customer key control. Can Redwood support on-prem key stores or BYOK?
[13:16] Maya Chen: Short answer: yes. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and on-prem deployments for regulated workloads. We integrate with common cloud KMS and can support HSMs for enterprise. We also export audit logs and have SSO/SAML + SCIM.
[13:40] Priya Singh: Great; please share the SOC2 report and the KMS integration guide.

[16:20] Luca Ramirez: Now some details on Dedicated vs Hosted - Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and isolation. If you need consistent p95 latency we recommend Dedicated with pinned models and prewarmed KV caches. Hosted is faster to get started and lower up-front cost.
[16:42] Jon Miller: For our scale, we have bursts during peak indexing windows. Autoscaling behaviour matters - do you have burst capacity?
[16:52] Luca Ramirez: Yes, Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling policies and burst capacity. Also Router policies can send overflow to hosted or alternate model variants.

[19:00] Alyssa Park: Cost parity - can you give rough token cost estimate vs OpenAI? We run ~10M tokens/month across chat and embedding.
[19:12] Maya Chen: We'll send a customized pricing estimate in the parity spreadsheet. Generally you can expect lower unit costs when using quantized model variants and batching; Redwood Optimize suggestions often reduce per-token cost by 20-40% depending on workload.

[22:30] Jon Miller: Quality regressions are a concern - do you have eval tooling to compare outputs and catch regressions?
[22:40] Luca Ramirez: Yes, Redwood has first-class eval tooling. You can run baseline prompts across model variants and get metrics (pass@k, rouge, custom metrics). We also tie regression alerts to prompt sets and historical baselines.

[25:05] Maya Chen: Quick demo: switching an OpenAI chat call to Redwood - example mapping: replace openai.com/v1/chat/completions with redwood.ai/v1/generate, keep messages array, pass functions as same schema, expect streaming events. I'll post the exact snippet after the call.
[25:28] Jon Miller: Any SDKs for Node/Python? We use Node for frontend and Python for backend pipelines.
[25:34] Luca Ramirez: Yes, Node and Python SDKs with the tokenizer helpers and examples for common transformations (OpenAI -> Redwood).

[28:50] Priya Singh: Data residency - our data must not leave EU for certain customers. Can we lock region?
[29:00] Maya Chen: Yes, you can pin region routing and deploy Private in customer VPCs for EU-only processing. We'll include architecture notes for VPC + private control plane.

[31:15] Alyssa Park: About function/tool calling - Together has a particular callback style; will our existing logic require major changes?
[31:28] Luca Ramirez: Function calling semantics are similar; Redwood supports the same call/response pattern but there are minor differences in the event stream. We provide an adapter snippet. Most customers get away with small changes.

[34:00] Jon Miller: We'll want to run a side-by-side: same prompts, same temps, measure latency, token usage, and output similarity.
[34:10] Luca Ramirez: Absolutely. For the PoC we'll run three targets: parity (feature parity), perf (latency/throughput), and quality (evaluation suite you provide). We recommend a 1-week perf baseline then 1-week tuned run.

[37:25] Maya Chen: Redwood Optimize recommendations - for heavy inference workloads we suggest: intelligent batching, prefix caching for repeated prompts, and using quantized variants where quality tests pass. Optimize can surface batch sizes and cache TTLs per-route.
[37:48] Alyssa Park: How much work to convert our existing batching pipeline? We currently batch at application layer.
[37:55] Luca Ramirez: You can keep application-level batching or hand it off - Redwood's continuous batching can handle many patterns; sometimes you simplify code by moving batching into the platform. We'll show config examples.

[40:30] Priya Singh: A few compliance questions - retention windows, deletion APIs, and audit log retention length.
[40:38] Maya Chen: Retention windows are configurable; we provide deletion APIs and verifiable deletion for Private deployments. Audit logs can be exported to your SIEM and retention can be increased with an add-on. We'll include specifics in the security pack.

[44:05] Jon Miller: Any gotchas with KV cache when moving models? We store long context for multi-turn assistants.
[44:14] Luca Ramirez: KV cache semantics vary by architecture; we map session ids and provide a migration guide to persist/rehydrate KV state. For very long contexts we recommend chunked retrieval and selective cache eviction.

[47:50] Alyssa Park: Sounds good. A few asks before we sign up for a PoC: 1) parity spreadsheet, 2) initial latency benchmark with our prompts, 3) security docs.
[47:59] Maya Chen: We'll deliver all three. I'll own the parity spreadsheet deliverable and Luca will run the benchmark. Priya you mentioned a compliance review - we'll send SOC 2 + KMS docs.

[50:10] Priya Singh: Please include details about BYOK and HSM options in the packet.
[50:18] Maya Chen: Will do. Also attaching a demo recording and code snippets in the followup.

[52:00] Alyssa Park: Rough timeline - if we get the parity doc and benchmarks this week we can decide on PoC next week.
[52:10] Maya Chen: Perfect. We'll aim to share parity doc by 2026-05-21 and schedule the PoC for week of 2026-05-31.
[53:00] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and next steps.
[53:05] Jon Miller: Thanks, appreciate it.
[53:10] Meeting ends.
